sections.h2: What makes San Antonio different from a small town sale?
sections.html:
San Antonio sits at the head of the San Antonio River in Bexar County, and its reach across the region is shaped by three interstates and two loops.

The Texas State Historical Association points to Interstate 10 running east and west, Interstates 35 and 37 running north and south, plus Loop 410, State Loop 1604, the international airport and daily Amtrak service. The Handbook describes about three centuries of history, starting with a presidio, a town and five Franciscan missions strung along the river, and notes that San Antonio was the biggest city in Texas through the later 1800s. Nicknames such as Alamo City, River City and Military City, U.S.A. reflect that story. The Handbook also lists the international airport and Stinson Airport among the facilities serving the city. Size is the practical lesson for a seller, because blocks inside and outside the loops can differ enormously in age, price and commute.

  • Compare recent sales within a mile or two of your house, not citywide numbers.
  • Note whether your house lies inside Loop 410, between the loops or beyond 1604.
  • Look at flood maps if the lot is close to the river or a creek.

sections.h2: Which way of selling fits a San Antonio house?
sections.html:
A broker listing rewards a sound house and patience, and an investor sale rewards a house needing work or a firm deadline.

A city this big produces a wide range of buyers and bids. Retail sales often yield the top figure and bring inspections, showings and lender conditions along. An owner sale skips the commission and loads marketing and paperwork on you. Investors buy as-is on a date you set, with the number trimmed for repair and resale expense. Compare each written bid by what you net after costs.

  • Listing: updated house, flexible date.
  • Investor sale: lien, empty inherited house or tenant trouble.
  • Before signing, read who pays title, recording and repair credits.

sections.h2: Who appraises and bills property tax in San Antonio?
sections.html:
Two offices touch your bill: BCAD decides the value, and the Bexar County Tax Assessor-Collector collects.

BCAD's front page states that it takes no tax payments and refers payment questions to the assessor-collector. A banner there says 2026 notices went to new owners and to owners whose value rose $1,000 or more, and adds that a protest needs no notice. The valuation date is January 1 statewide, bills arrive in October and the payment deadline is January 31. Every taxing unit on your lot sets a rate of its own.

sections.h2: Which dates should a San Antonio owner keep in mind?
sections.html:
Five milestones frame the year for a Bexar County owner.

Texas property tax schedule as it applies to Bexar County owners (Texas Comptroller)
DateWhat it means
January 1Valuation date and lien date
April 30Common exemption filing cutoff
May 15Usual protest deadline
July 20Review board approves appraisal records
September 29Deadline for most units to adopt rates
February 1Delinquency begins on unpaid taxes

The full list is on the Comptroller calendar.

sections.h2: How do I handle back taxes before selling in San Antonio?
sections.html:
Get the amount due from the Bexar County Tax Assessor-Collector and plan to settle it by closing, since the lien does not leave with you.

Delinquency opens at 6 percent penalty plus 1 percent interest in February and reaches a 12 percent penalty in July while interest continues. Collection lawyers can add up to a fifth more. Homestead owners may request an installment plan, which some offices extend to 36 months. A lawsuit can lead to a tax sale, and surplus proceeds can be claimed by the former owner for two years.

  • While appealing a value, pay at least the part nobody disputes.
  • Save each receipt.
  • Let the closer know about any plan.

sections.h2: What homestead relief could a San Antonio owner claim?
sections.html:
Owners can claim the residence homestead exemption, with added relief for age, disability or veteran status.

Schools take $140,000 off a homestead and a further $60,000 off for seniors and the disabled. A taxing unit may add its own exemption of up to 20 percent of value, floor $5,000. A yearly cap of 10 percent limits growth in a homestead's appraised value. Veterans receive $5,000 to $12,000 by rating, and a full 100 percent rating gives a total homestead exemption. Heirs missing from the recorded deed show an affidavit, a death certificate and a recent utility bill.

sections.h2: What do squatters and holdover occupants mean for a San Antonio sale?
sections.html:
Someone who stays after being told to go can be removed by a justice court case or, narrowly, by a request to the sheriff or constable under Property Code chapter 24B.

That shortcut requires a refusal to leave, a property that was closed to the public at entry, no pending suit between the two of you, and an occupant who is no relative and no past or present tenant. Wrongful removal exposes the owner to suit. Tenants usually get three days' notice, and a writ of possession waits for judgment plus six days.

sections.h2: How is a San Antonio deed recorded?
sections.html:
Deeds for Bexar County land are filed with the clerk, and a notary or similar officer must attest the signature first.

The clerk manual puts the first page at $5.00 and later pages at $4.00, plus other records fees. The title company usually files.

sections.h2: What can a Bexar County heir do with an inherited house?
sections.html:
Heirs have several routes to clear title, and the right one depends on what the owner left behind and what the house owes.

With a will, the executor or an heir files it for probate, which Texas permits for four years after death. If no administration is needed, a muniment of title order and the will go on record with the county clerk. Without a will, a small estate affidavit may work for modest estates. A deed that names a beneficiary and was recorded before the owner's death moves the house outside probate, and a Lady Bird deed lets the owner keep selling rights while alive. Expect the closer to ask for whichever paper applies.

  • Get certified copies of the death certificate.
  • Find the last recorded deed for the parcel.
  • Ask the appraisal district about the homestead exemption before the next tax year.

sections.h2: How does a Texas foreclosure reach a San Antonio house?
sections.html:
Most Texas mortgages allow a sale without a court case, which makes the timeline short.

Federal rules generally hold a servicer back until a home loan is more than 120 days behind. A default notice then opens a 20 day period to bring the loan current, and the sale notice must be sent, posted at the courthouse and filed with the clerk at least 21 days before the auction. The auction itself takes place on a first Tuesday, with the first Wednesday used if that Tuesday is January 1 or July 4. Selling before that date can preserve equity and spare you a foreclosure on your record.

faqs.q: Which office collects San Antonio property tax?
faqs.a: The Bexar County Tax Assessor-Collector. The Bexar Central Appraisal District says it does not accept payments.

faqs.q: Do I need a notice to protest my value in San Antonio?
faqs.a: No. The Bexar Central Appraisal District says you do not need a notice to submit a protest. Check your notice for the cutoff, which most years falls in mid May.

faqs.q: What homestead exemption do school districts give?
faqs.a: A $140,000 deduction from value, with $60,000 more for owners who are seniors or disabled.

faqs.q: What happens to the lien when a San Antonio house sells?
faqs.a: It remains on the house, so any old tax is deducted at closing.

faqs.q: When do foreclosure auctions occur near San Antonio?
faqs.a: On a first Tuesday, during daytime hours, after a sale notice at least three weeks earlier.
